body: The spec is largely a faithful elaboration of the idea, but it commits one serious error of logic and several smaller ones. First, SC-001 is not a success criterion at all — it is a demand that the phenomenon exist. Requiring Cohen's d ≥ 0.3 with p < 0.05 in ≥ 80% of 1,000 bootstrap resamples makes a genuine null result (which the idea explicitly anticipates as an acceptable outcome, option b) a project failure. A success criterion should measure whether the pipeline correctly detects or correctly fails to detect an effect; as written it biases the work toward a positive finding and violates the spec's own Principle II ('No claim shall exceed the evidential support of the observational data'). Second, FR-009's exclusion trigger — 'grid interpolation reliability is < 95%' — is a number with no defined measurement procedure; what quantity, computed how, yields a reliability of 95%? Either define it or drop it. Third, US-1's independent test anchors validation on 'the 2018 Alaska subset (N=12)', a count asserted nowhere else and unverifiable from the artifact; a validation test built on an unexplained magic number is no test. Fourth, FR-003's 'left-censored 30-day moving average (excluding the event window and a preceding baseline period)' quietly changes the idea's plain 30-day moving average into a more complex estimator whose censoring window is unspecified in length — the number that matters is missing. Finally, FR-011's ENSO/PDO stratification is a genuine improvement over the idea's crude same-date-different-year controls, and the block-permutation scheme in FR-004 is sound; these deserve credit. But fix SC-001 before implementation, or the pipeline will be under institutional pressure to find what may not be there.
